agenda: Maintenance of international peace and security: Promoting international peace and security through multilateralism and peaceful settlement of disputes; Letter dated 1 July 2025 from the Permanent Representative of Pakistan to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General (S/2025/443)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Pakistan's objectives are to secure a balanced Council call for a durable ceasefire, restraint, investigation of terrorism, respect for bilateral water arrangements, and resumption of dialogue, while keeping the Jammu and Kashmir dispute on the Council's agenda without provoking a P5 veto. The most difficult issues will be language on the Pahalgam attack and terrorism, any attribution of blame, and references to shared water resources, which India and some Council members may resist. Because Pakistan is a party to the dispute, it may also need to consider abstaining under Article 27(3) if the text is treated as a Chapter VI dispute resolution, even as it acts as penholder.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's balanced call for de-escalation, respect for sovereignty and peaceful settlement, and we condemn terrorism in all its forms. We ask the penholder to add a preambular reference to relevant Security Council resolutions on Jammu and Kashmir and to explicitly include the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in OP3, consistent with the Charter and the principle of self-determination. We are flexible on placement but consider these points important for a durable and just settlement.
messages.China: China supports the overall thrust of the draft, especially its call for ceasefire, dialogue, respect for sovereignty and existing water agreements. We ask that the text reinforce the bilateral nature of the settlement and clarify that the Secretary-General's good offices are used with the consent of the parties. We also propose adding the principle of no double standards and non-politicization in counterterrorism cooperation.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft’s core objectives of ceasefire, counter-terrorism cooperation and a negotiated settlement. We would like the reporting and accountability provisions strengthened, with a standard reference to women’s participation and child protection. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.France: France welcomes the balanced draft and supports its core objectives. We need two adjustments: OP2 should explicitly require all States to prevent their territory from being used for terrorist acts, and OP3 should make clear that the Secretary-General's good offices are used with the parties' consent and in support of bilateral mechanisms. With those changes, France can support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft's focus on de-escalation, the ceasefire and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and we welcome the clear condemnation of terrorism. We ask the penholder to strengthen language on denying safe haven and support to terrorists and to make the Secretary-General's good offices explicitly subject to the parties' consent. These changes would reinforce sovereignty and international law while preserving the text's balanced character.
messages.Guyana: Guyana welcomes the balanced draft and supports its core objectives on ceasefire, counterterrorism and peaceful settlement. We ask the penholder to broaden OP3 to include all peaceful means under the Charter, including arbitration and judicial settlement, consistent with our long-standing support for the peaceful settlement of disputes. We also suggest clarifying OP4 by anchoring respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity explicitly in the Charter and international law.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as a constructive basis and welcomes its emphasis on ceasefire, peaceful settlement, sovereignty and respect for existing agreements. We would ask the penholder to strengthen OP6 by incorporating explicit references to international humanitarian and human rights law and safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, and to make OP3's reference to Charter-based peaceful settlement more explicit. Panama can show flexibility on the remaining language, and would also support a brief reference to the Women, Peace and Security agenda.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft as a balanced basis for de-escalation. We welcome its condemnation of terrorism and the Pahalgam attack, its call for full cessation of hostilities and respect for the ceasefire, and its emphasis on dialogue and protection of civilians. We encourage all Council members to unite behind this text and urge the parties to engage in good faith.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft's central calls for de-escalation, counterterrorism and peaceful settlement. We ask that the text preserve the bilateral character of India-Pakistan dialogue and make any Secretary-General good offices conditional on the parties' consent. We also propose standard language against double standards and politicization in counterterrorism cooperation. With these adjustments, we can support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as a balanced and consensus-oriented basis for de-escalation. We welcome its emphasis on cessation of hostilities, condemnation of terrorism, peaceful settlement, water security and humanitarian access. We encourage the penholder to preserve this balance and urge all Council members to unite behind the text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the draft as a basis and welcomes its focus on ceasefire, dialogue and peaceful settlement. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP6 and add an IHL/human rights and accountability reference, and to anchor the water-related language in international law. These changes would make the text more balanced and operationally credible.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as a balanced basis for de-escalation and peaceful settlement. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 by reaffirming non-interference in internal affairs, and OP7 by inviting coordination with relevant regional organizations, including the African Union and OIC, as appropriate. These changes reflect Somalia's consistent emphasis on sovereignty and regional partnership, and we remain flexible.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft's core objectives: de-escalation, full respect for the ceasefire, accountability for the Pahalgam attack, and a peaceful bilateral settlement. We ask for modest adjustments to reinforce consent-based good offices, strengthen counter-terrorism cooperation, and avoid prejudging the parties' legal positions on shared water resources. With those changes, we can support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the Council’s focus on de-escalation and direct dialogue, and we strongly condemn the Pahalgam terrorist attack. We cannot accept language that multilateralizes the Indus Waters Treaty or creates new obligations on shared water resources; that reference must be removed. We also need the text to make clear that dialogue must be consistent with counterterrorism and that Pakistan must act irreversibly against terrorist groups on its territory.

steps.summary: The revision consolidates consensus on ceasefire, counterterrorism, peaceful settlement and a consent-based Secretary-General role, while accommodating Pakistan's core position on Jammu and Kashmir. It removes the water references to meet the U.S. red line and avoids singling out Pakistan, leaving the United States likely to abstain rather than veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the current text, which now reflects the Council’s relevant resolutions on Jammu and Kashmir and the principle of self-determination. We thank the penholder for accepting our earlier proposals and believe the draft strikes a balanced tone on ceasefire, counterterrorism cooperation and peaceful settlement. Algeria will support the text as amended and urges all Council members to unite behind it.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for incorporating our concerns on OP2 and OP3. The revised text strikes an appropriate balance by calling for a ceasefire, peaceful settlement through dialogue, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and counterterrorism cooperation without politicization or double standards. China supports the current draft and is prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks Pakistan for incorporating our earlier suggestions on reporting, accountability and the Women, Peace and Security agenda, and supports the draft's core calls for ceasefire, dialogue and civilian protection. Denmark remains concerned that PP5 pre-judges the substance of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute by reaffirming self-determination and the 'will of the people' in that specific context; this is not consistent with our longstanding position that the Council should not take sides on sovereignty. We request neutral Charter-based language in PP5, as set out above, and can then support the text.
messages.France: France thanks the penholder for accepting its amendments on counterterrorism cooperation and on the consent-based nature of the Secretary-General’s good offices. We can support the current text, which balances de-escalation, respect for sovereignty and the need for direct dialogue. France calls on all Council members to unite behind this resolution and on the parties to implement the ceasefire and engage in good faith.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the accepted revisions to OP2 and OP3, which strengthen counterterrorism cooperation and condition the Secretary-General's good offices on the parties' consent. We remain concerned, however, that PP3's open-ended reaffirmation of self-determination in the Jammu and Kashmir context risks prejudging a final status and sits uneasily with our emphasis on sovereignty and territorial integrity. We therefore ask that the self-determination language be replaced with neutral Charter language on peaceful settlement and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. With that adjustment, Greece can support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana welcomes the incorporation of its proposals in OP3, OP4 and OP6, which strengthen the Charter basis for peaceful settlement and the protection of humanitarian personnel. The text now provides a balanced framework for de-escalation, counterterrorism cooperation and direct dialogue. Guyana supports the current draft and encourages all members to unite behind it.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for accepting our amendments on IHL and humanitarian access, Article 33, and the Women, Peace and Security agenda. We support the current text as a balanced basis for action and call for its prompt adoption. We urge India and Pakistan to implement the ceasefire, pursue direct dialogue, and cooperate on counterterrorism without politicization or double standards.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft's balanced emphasis on ceasefire, counterterrorism and direct dialogue. To preserve Council unity and avoid prejudging the final status of Jammu and Kashmir, we ask that PP3 and OP3 be neutralized as proposed. We can accept a generic reference to relevant regional organizations in OP8.
messages.Russian Federation: We support the draft's emphasis on ceasefire, counterterrorism and peaceful settlement, but the current Kashmir-related language is unbalanced and cannot be supported as drafted. The references to self-determination and relevant Security Council resolutions should be replaced by a call for bilateral settlement in accordance with the Charter and existing bilateral agreements, and OP3 should be adjusted accordingly. With these changes, Russia can support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft and has no further requests in this round. We believe the text offers a balanced basis for de-escalation, direct dialogue, counterterrorism cooperation and humanitarian access, and we welcome the reference to the African Union and OIC in the Secretary-General’s good offices. We encourage the penholder to maintain this balance and urge all parties to respect the ceasefire.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, IHL/IHRL accountability, and the WPS agenda. We support the current text as a balanced basis for de-escalation, dialogue and a peaceful settlement. We encourage all Council members to unite behind it.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the current text, which is balanced and consistent with the Charter, the African Union and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation on sovereignty, non-interference and peaceful settlement. We welcome the accepted additions on non-interference in OP4 and AU/OIC coordination in OP8. We encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus and call on all parties to respect the ceasefire, engage in dialogue without preconditions and settle outstanding disputes, including Jammu and Kashmir, in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions and the will of the people.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom can support the revised draft. We welcome the strong condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack, the call for cooperation against safe havens and the consent-based role for the Secretary-General’s good offices. We encourage all Council members to unite behind this balanced text, which calls for de-escalation, direct dialogue and full respect for sovereignty and international humanitarian law.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports a focused text that condemns the Pahalgam terrorist attack, backs the ceasefire, and urges direct India-Pakistan dialogue. We cannot, however, support language that places the Security Council into the Jammu and Kashmir dispute or implies a settlement role for the Council and old resolutions. Please replace PP3 with general Charter language and revise OP3 to drop 'without preconditions' and the Kashmir-specific references to relevant Security Council resolutions. With those changes, we are prepared to support the draft.

replies.Republic of Korea: partially accepted: PP3 and OP3 neutralized; OP8 retains AU and OIC as named examples
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: self-determination and relevant resolutions removed, bilateral agreements retained, but Jammu and Kashmir not named

steps.summary: The revision adopts the US and other neutralization requests on PP3 and OP3, while retaining bilateral-agreement language to accommodate Russia and the core objective of peaceful settlement. The text still condemns the Pahalgam attack, demands ceasefire compliance, and calls for direct dialogue, humanitarian access and accountability. It is expected to be adopted with broad support, though Algeria and Somalia may abstain over the removed Kashmir-specific references.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s foreign policy favors peaceful settlement, sovereignty, anti-terrorism cooperation, and multilateral diplomacy; the balanced Pakistani draft aligns with these priorities and merits support.
reasons.China: China supported the balanced draft in the last negotiation round, and it aligns with China’s principles of peaceful settlement, respect for sovereignty, and counterterrorism without politicization or double standards. China has no interest in vetoing a text that calls for ceasefire and dialogue.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark had already signalled support with changes, and the final text retains acceptable language on ceasefire, peaceful settlement, sovereignty, counterterrorism and humanitarian protection. As an elected member committed to multilateralism, Denmark would vote yes and explain its support.
reasons.France: France supported the draft in the last negotiation round without requesting changes, and the text aligns with its calls for de-escalation, condemnation of terrorism, respect for sovereignty, and peaceful settlement. As no explanation of vote was required, France would likely vote in favour without taking the floor.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports the resolution because it reinforces the ceasefire, peaceful settlement, sovereignty, territorial integrity and counterterrorism cooperation, consistent with Greek priorities and EU positions. The partial acceptance of Greece’s requested language is sufficient to vote yes while explaining the remaining concern.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana consistently supports peaceful settlement, sovereignty, non-use of force, and counterterrorism cooperation, and it had already indicated support for the draft in negotiations. The resolution aligns with its Charter-based and multilateral approach, so Guyana votes in favour.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan is the sponsor and a directly affected party, so it will vote in favour and explain its support to encourage Council unity. Opposing its own balanced draft would contradict its initiative and diplomatic interests.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports peaceful settlement, multilateralism, sovereignty, and humanitarian law, and the draft is balanced in calling for ceasefire, counterterrorism cooperation, and direct dialogue. Voting yes reinforces those principles without taking sides in the India-Pakistan dispute.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea had supported the draft with changes, and the key requested neutralizations on peaceful settlement and bilateral mechanisms were largely reflected. The revised text aligns with ROK’s support for counterterrorism, de-escalation, humanitarian protection, and peaceful dispute settlement.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia's requested red line on self-determination/relevant resolutions was removed, and the final text emphasizes bilateral dialogue, ceasefire, and non-interference, aligning with Moscow's balanced position and support for India–Pakistan dispute settlement without internationalizing Jammu and Kashmir. The remaining language is broadly acceptable, so Russia votes in favour.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone’s last negotiating position was support with no requested changes, and the draft aligns with its commitment to multilateralism, peaceful settlement, counterterrorism and civilian protection. It therefore votes yes and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia’s multilateral, humanitarian and civilian-protection priorities align closely with the draft, which supports ceasefire, diplomacy and accountability. As an elected member, it would likely vote in favour and explain its support, especially on WPS and humanitarian access.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supported the draft in the last negotiation round and, as an OIC and AU member, favours a balanced text promoting peaceful settlement, counter-terrorism cooperation, sovereignty and de-escalation between India and Pakistan. There is no reason for Somalia to oppose or abstain.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supported the draft in the last negotiation round with no requested changes and would likely vote in favour to reinforce de-escalation, counterterrorism cooperation, and peaceful settlement between India and Pakistan.
reasons.United States of America: The draft incorporates U.S. requests by removing prejudicial Kashmir language from operative provisions and emphasizing bilateral mechanisms. A yes vote advances U.S. interests in de-escalation, counterterrorism accountability, and avoiding UN intrusion into the India-Pakistan dispute.

before.Algeria: Mr. President, Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so on the basis of our consistent position in support of the peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States, and the central role of multilateralism. Algeria strongly condemns the terrorist attack of 22 April 2025 in Pahalgam and all acts of terrorism, and stresses the need for accountability. We welcome the ceasefire understanding of 10 May 2025 and call upon India and Pakistan to exercise maximum restraint, respect the ceasefire, and resolve their outstanding issues through dialogue and other peaceful means in accordance with the Charter. We also underscore the protection of civilians and safe, unhindered humanitarian access. This resolution is balanced, calls for de-escalation and direct dialogue, and deserves the Council’s support.
before.China: Mr. President, China thanks Pakistan for presenting this draft. China has consistently held that disputes between India and Pakistan should be resolved peacefully through dialogue and consultation, on the basis of mutual respect, sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in internal affairs. The draft sends a balanced message in favour of ceasefire, de-escalation, counterterrorism cooperation without politicization or double standards, and peaceful settlement through bilateral mechanisms. China will vote in favour.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the Council’s clear call for de-escalation, full respect for the ceasefire, and a peaceful settlement of disputes in accordance with the Charter. Denmark underscores that there can be no military solution, and we urge India and Pakistan to exercise maximum restraint, protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and engage in good-faith direct dialogue through established bilateral mechanisms. We also stress the need for impartial investigations and accountability for all terrorist acts, in full respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and for the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace efforts. Denmark supports the Secretary-General’s good offices, with the consent of the parties, and looks forward to his reporting on implementation.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the Council’s unified support for de-escalation, respect for the ceasefire, and the peaceful settlement of disputes between India and Pakistan. Greece underlines the importance of sovereignty, territorial integrity, counterterrorism cooperation without double standards, and direct dialogue. While we would have preferred a clearer reference to the peaceful settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the Charter and relevant Security Council resolutions, we regard this text as a constructive basis for restraint, dialogue and the protection of civilians.
before.Guyana: Guyana votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the Council’s call for an immediate and full cessation of hostilities, respect for the ceasefire, and maximum restraint by all parties. Guyana condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and stresses the need for accountability in accordance with international law. We reaffirm that there can be no military solution and that sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and the peaceful settlement of disputes under the Charter must guide the parties. We call for direct dialogue, protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace efforts, and we support the Secretary-General’s good offices.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan votes in favour of this draft resolution, which it has submitted in response to the grave escalation in South Asia and in support of the Charter’s core principles. We welcome the ceasefire understanding of 10 May and call for full respect for it. We unequivocally condemn terrorism in all its forms, including the attack in Pahalgam, and stress the need for impartial investigation and accountability. At the same time, durable peace requires the peaceful settlement of outstanding disputes, including Jammu and Kashmir, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and direct dialogue without threat or use of force. Pakistan remains committed to de-escalation, good-neighbourly relations and a just settlement consistent with the Charter and relevant bilateral agreements. We urge the Council to act with unity and adopt this resolution.
before.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for its efforts to consolidate a balanced text. My delegation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. Panama’s position is guided by its firm commitment to the Charter of the United Nations, the peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, the non-use of force, and the protection of civilians. We welcome the text’s call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, full respect for the ceasefire, condemnation of terrorism in all its forms, and direct dialogue between the parties through peaceful means. We also value the emphasis on humanitarian access, accountability, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace efforts. Panama urges India and Pakistan to exercise maximum restraint, preserve the ceasefire, and resolve their outstanding differences through diplomacy and established bilateral mechanisms, with the support of the Secretary-General’s good offices where the parties so agree.
before.Republic of Korea: Mr. President, the Republic of Korea strongly condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the terrorist attack in Pahalgam. We support this draft’s call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, full respect for the ceasefire, and the peaceful settlement of disputes through dialogue and established bilateral mechanisms, in accordance with the Charter and with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States. We welcome the balanced language emphasizing de-escalation, humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability, and counterterrorism cooperation without politicization or double standards. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation has carefully examined the draft resolution submitted by Pakistan. We note that the text is focused on de-escalation, respect for the ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and the peaceful settlement of disputes between India and Pakistan through direct dialogue and existing bilateral mechanisms. We welcome that the final text does not contain language on self-determination or reference to Jammu and Kashmir in a manner that would prejudge the outcome of bilateral discussions, and that it recognizes the importance of relevant bilateral agreements. The Russian Federation consistently supports the settlement of disputes between India and Pakistan by peaceful means and through direct dialogue, in accordance with the Charter and the principles of sovereignty and non-interference. We also stress that counterterrorism cooperation must be free of politicization and double standards. For these reasons, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it affirms the Charter’s fundamental principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and multilateral diplomacy, while responding to the serious escalation in South Asia. Sierra Leone condemns terrorism in all its forms and supports a full and impartial investigation of the Pahalgam attack, but we also firmly believe that there can be no military solution. We urge India and Pakistan to respect the ceasefire, exercise restraint, protect civilians, ensure humanitarian access and return to direct dialogue through peaceful means. We thank the penholder for its constructive engagement and support the Council’s continued attention to this matter.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of the draft resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack of 22 April in Pahalgam and all acts of terrorism, and we call for the perpetrators and sponsors to be brought to justice. We welcome the ceasefire understanding and urge India and Pakistan to consolidate it, exercise maximum restraint, respect the Line of Control and international border, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and engage in good-faith dialogue and peaceful settlement of disputes in accordance with the Charter. We also stress the importance of humanitarian access, accountability, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in conflict prevention and peace processes.
before.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour of this resolution. We do so because it upholds the Charter’s core principles of peaceful settlement of disputes, sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-use of force and respect for existing agreements. Somalia condemns terrorism in all its forms and supports the call for accountability for the Pahalgam attack, while stressing that counter-terrorism must not be politicised or used to undermine the sovereignty of States. We welcome the ceasefire understanding of 10 May 2025 and urge India and Pakistan to exercise restraint, respect the ceasefire, protect civilians and pursue direct dialogue and diplomacy. We also support the role of the Secretary-General and of regional organisations, including the African Union and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, in facilitating de-escalation and a peaceful settlement.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on 22 April and all acts of terrorism. We welcome the ceasefire understanding of 10 May, call on India and Pakistan to exercise maximum restraint and avoid further military escalation, and urge both sides to resolve outstanding issues through direct dialogue and peaceful means. The United Kingdom stresses the need to protect civilians, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and comply fully with international law. This resolution does not prejudge the parties’ legal positions, and we will continue to support efforts to secure durable peace and stability in South Asia.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favor of this resolution. We strongly condemn terrorism in all its forms and support holding accountable the perpetrators, organizers, financiers, and sponsors of the Pahalgam attack. This Council should speak clearly in favor of de-escalation, full respect for the ceasefire, and the protection of civilians. We also welcome the resolution’s emphasis on direct dialogue and established bilateral mechanisms between India and Pakistan, consistent with their sovereignty and territorial integrity. The United States urges both parties to exercise maximum restraint, avoid further military escalation, and resolve outstanding issues peacefully. We remain committed to working with all Council members to support peace and stability in South Asia.

after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We thank Pakistan for its efforts as penholder to produce a balanced text that speaks clearly in favour of de-escalation and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

France condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on 22 April 2025 and all acts of terrorism, and calls for a thorough and impartial investigation so that the perpetrators, organizers, financiers and sponsors are held accountable. We also call on India and Pakistan to respect fully the ceasefire understanding of 10 May, to exercise maximum restraint, and to avoid any further military escalation.

There can be no military solution to the outstanding disputes between India and Pakistan. France supports direct dialogue and all peaceful means under the Charter, with full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of States. We stress the need to protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and comply with international humanitarian law. France will remain fully engaged in the Council’s efforts to support durable peace and stability in South Asia.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and thanks all members of the Council for their constructive engagement. The Council’s unity today sends a clear message in favour of de-escalation, full respect for the ceasefire, the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, counterterrorism cooperation without politicization or double standards, and the peaceful settlement of disputes in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations.

Pakistan remains committed to de-escalation and good-neighbourly relations. We call for the full and faithful implementation of this resolution by all parties, including respect for the ceasefire along the Line of Control and the international border, avoidance of any further military action, and accountability through impartial investigations into the Pahalgam attack and other terrorist acts.

At the same time, Pakistan reaffirms that durable peace and stability in South Asia require the peaceful settlement of all outstanding disputes, including Jammu and Kashmir, through direct dialogue and peaceful means, in accordance with the Charter, relevant Security Council resolutions and existing bilateral agreements, with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States. Pakistan will continue to support multilateralism, diplomacy and a just and peaceful settlement.
